stratum_definition: C1_P0_early_stop is initial C1 PASS; repair_feedback is its complement; both are defined before generation
rng: Python standard-library random.Random; one stream, all_tasks then repair_feedback; random.choices(range(n), k=n) per bootstrap draw
paired_indices: The same draw is applied to every service and metric within a stratum; each stratum is resampled internally and independently in the stream
missingness: retain all 29 tasks including task 989 local refusals; assert complete PASS/FAIL endpoint pairs and known usage; fail rather than silently discard unknown or missing values
validation: Verify exact source digest and source-analysis identity
Verify 522 unique logical rows, 29 task identities, two services, three policies, and three repetitions
Check primary point estimates against the published counts and token totals
Check six-task and 23-task weighted decomposition equals the 29-task estimate
Compare type-7 interval endpoints against statistics.quantiles(n=40, method=inclusive)
Compare bootstrap mean and variance against the exact empirical-bootstrap mean/variance of a task mean; retain degenerate metrics explicitly
interpretation: Intervals describe task-resampling uncertainty conditional on the selected C0-failure cohort, fixed policies, observations, and three collected repetitions
They do not repair selection bias, imply a random sample of all defects, measure uncertainty of the fully observed finite cohort, or establish a general C0/C1 ranking
Tasks are exchangeability units for resampling, not a claim that task families are independent or representative
No new within-task model randomness is simulated; online Kimi service drift is not covered
Intervals are pointwise and exploratory, not simultaneous or multiplicity-adjusted; no null-hypothesis or equivalence tests are performed
Tokens and HTTP durations remain provider-specific logical cost components; they are not currency, pure inference time, end-to-end latency, or additive physical billing
